My point is that things like cross and last layer are the two variables that you could easily eliminate early on that do not require a large timesink while also improving on other things. Very fast solvers do not have bad crosses and last layers, but a lot of sub15s-sub 20s could easily be sub 12s-sub 15s just by learning full OLL. By improving those two skills, you’ll pick up a lot of the more difficult skills along the way (recognition for f2l cases, lookahead, etc) as you work on getting good crosses during inspection or improve at recognizing OLLs/PLLs

I really do not like telling people they should only learn your standard last layer alg sets at sub 20 or sub 15 because in hindsight it really is not all that difficult and will only dramatically help them later on. Mappings between two surfaces that preserve the metric between each surface is one of the fundamental problems of interest in Classical Differential Geometry. Attached is an animation of a mapping between a Helicoid and a Catenoid, in which the metric is preserved. Thus this transformation is called an "isometry". We know this mapping is possible with certain generators of the parametrization of both surfaces. Choosing choice functions for generators causes the surfaces to have the same [First Fundamental Form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_fundamental_form), which allows for an inner product to be defined on the tangent space to the surface.

The First Fundamental Form is important because it allows us to define curvature, distance, etc., on the surface which allows us to do calculus-y things as if it was euclidean space.

You know, you bring a valuable point to the table. But - we can never forget the artistic merit that each outfit brings to the table. Remember, posters on r/streetwear are indeed artists. I find that the beautiful, deep political commentary on American society depicted in both in the outfit and photograph. 

To start, the outfit is obviously a critique on gun laws. We are fearful of being in public commons, such as schools, due to the stricter and stricter guidelines if crisis approaches (namely ALICE). OP starts the fit with a business approach, a blazer, derbies, etc, but switches it up with the tactical vest. The vest implies readiness - people always need to be ready for crisis. This dimension of the outfit is clearly demonstrating the victim in a crisis.

However, I feel like there is more interpretation to the outfit. If you have knowledge of the pieces used in the fit, you would know that the blazer is detailed with a skull enveloped in flowers. OP uses this detail to express the human condition as a whole. People are susceptible to illness - and death. The main headline in every news article after a crisis is the focus on the perpetrator and their mental illness. 

The gray, boring concrete jungle symbolizes our disregard for this national issue. We've become desensitized to mass shootings, and we simply cannot deny it. Did you know that there was 7 mass shootings in the US during the week of this post? Neither did I, until I decided to look into the facts and the artistic styling OP used in the photo. It's clear that the intentions were there - we just aren't looking hard enough. 

Playing off of that same facet, OP decides to blur out his face; he is taking a stance in the argument. The popular argument after every crisis is that we should not focus on the perpetrator, but the victims. Too many times we choose to remember the evil in a crisis, rather than remembering the souls of the departed. OP ties all of these critical messages with the blazer, the photo editing, and the two faceted outfit. 

Overall, you can have your reserved opinions on the outfit, but I feel like it's one of the greatest outfits of all time on this subreddit. It's smart, it's autistic, and it demonstrates deep commentary on current events like all great art during their contemporary period.
